I have to head canon that this is a write-up from early days of initial containment.

Because the logical first test would be to scan it and see what's inside. The metal case would cause interference, but you should be able to get at least an idea if it's circuit boards or vacuum tubes or flesh or swirling bad vibes jammed in the box.

Also, they'd probably get more useful results with a restrained subject touching it and an unrelated doctor conducting the interview.

I'm sure they'll get to those tests in week two of the intake program.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
zhax__, just because it’s “immobile” and “harmless”, that doesn’t mean it is Safe. For God’s sake, it can speak.

Object class is based on difficulty of containment, so it's pretty reasonable to think that something that doesn't really do anything when it's locked up would be Safe class.

It has a mind of its own (I assume). That means it can be unpredictable, which falls it as Euclid.

Not necessarily. We have a couple Safe-class humanoids who definitely are sapient (not just sentient) but are pretty docile and/or rely on the Foundation a lot for basic wellbeing, such as SCP-134.

Some “well-known” Safe Classes mostly don’t have a brain, or, aren’t that smart enough to be really sentient. Here’s some examples. SCP-914, SCP-860, (forgot the number, “The Jaded Ring” or something like that), SCP-504, etc.

There are more articles on the site than just the well-known ones.

I personally think that this is a bit of a borderline case. I would have noted that the object is Safe-class, myself, but I can understand the motivation behind making it Euclid because apparently it can easily make a professional (or at least, someone who should be acting professional) staff member lose their composure really quickly and should be handled with caution during interaction/testing.

item.content:encoded:
I have a theory: Maybe this thing isn't sapient at all, or even alive - maybe it's just a reflection of a person's internal critic. As far as I can tell, it takes on whatever voice would be most irritating to whoever activates it, and then says exactly what its activator least wants to hear, in the worst possible way they could hear it. A person's darkest fears, what they secretly worry people say or think about them or do behind their back, all vocalized as fact by the most irritating, insulting voice possible…maybe that's all this thing is. It would certainly explain why the box insults people, and it would also explain the unexpectedly high adrenaline it induces - it's not just being insulting, it's saying, word for word, what people are most afraid of hearing.

Possibly?
